summary: The note surveys the growth of esports from a subculture into a global industry, covering revenue, audience demographics, economic impact, infrastructure, fan engagement, community and philanthropy, and future technology trends. It cites figures such as over $1.5 billion in projected 2024 revenue and a 495 million cumulative 2023 audience, and notes a younger, mostly male but increasingly diverse viewership. It closes with the potential of VR and AI and links to education and healthcare.
one_line: Overview of esports' rapid growth in revenue, audience, infrastructure, fan engagement and future technology, with key figures and events from 2023-2024.
key_facts: The Global Esports Market Report projects the esports industry will generate over $1.5 billion in revenue by 2024.
Esports had a cumulative viewership of over 495 million in 2023 alone.
A study published on January 15, 2024 found approximately 62% of esports viewers fall in the 18-35 age bracket.
Male viewers account for around 70% of the total esports audience, though female viewership and participation is rising.
Sponsorship and advertising revenue was estimated to reach upward of $800 million by the close of 2023, with Intel and Coca-Cola among the investors.
The Fortnite World Cup was held on December 10, 2023, combining live streaming and interactive viewer participation.
Cloud9 inaugurated its Los Angeles training facility on September 12, 2023.
The Esports Arena in Las Vegas exists, and the Esports Stadium Arlington in Texas is planned to open next year.
The International Dota 2 Championships on November 3, 2023 experimentally fused augmented reality elements into the viewing experience.
The charity tournament 'Gamers for Good' was held on January 20, 2024 to raise funds and awareness for various causes.
In-game drops give viewers items for watching events, and these items often have real-world monetary value.
Organizations use Discord and Twitter to build fan communities, while Twitch and YouTube broadcast key tournaments and leagues live.
VR and AI are expected to transform esports, with VR offering immersive spectating and AI offering in-depth analytics.
Educational institutions are integrating esports into curricula, and VR esports is being explored as a therapeutic and rehabilitative tool in healthcare.
